Maintenance Report — MNT-0044-003

Asset: WELL-0044 (SW-23 Well 044, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 10 Mar 2023 08:00 · Finished: 11 Mar 2023 06:00 · Well stopped for this job: 22 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0044-0021 on 2023-03-09 Report written: 13 Mar 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0044-0021 at 12:45 on 2023-03-09 found crude oil on the pad: about 8.9% of the pad area, estimated 4.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 284 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 227 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.1 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0044-003 (WS-06).

What happened

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0044-0053 showed the wellhead at 26.2 °C with the air at 21.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 7 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing. This is corrective repair number 4 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0044-026

Asset: WELL-0044 (SW-23 Well 044, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 09 May 2025 08:00 · Finished: 10 May 2025 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 29 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0044-0131 on 2025-05-08 Report written: 10 May 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0044-0131 at 13:00 on 2025-05-08 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.2% of the pad area, estimated 2.9 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.7 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 284 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 227 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0044-026 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.38% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
